lessons.title: Lesson 1: Introduction to PHP Syntax
lessons.html:
Lesson 1: Introduction to PHP Syntax

PHP (Hypertext Preprocessor) is a popular server-side scripting language that is widely used for web development.

Basic Syntax Elements:

  • The PHP Tag: Use
  • echo: A command to output data to the screen.

Example:

<?php echo Hello, World!; ?>

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Control Structures (Conditions and Loops)
lessons.html:
Lesson 2: Control Structures

Control structures allow you to direct the flow of execution in your code.

Conditions:

Use if, else, and switch to execute code based on conditions.

if ($a > $b) { echo a is greater than b; } else { echo b is greater than a; }

Loops:

For and while loops allow executing the same block of code multiple times.

for ($i = 0; $i < 5; $i++) { echo $i; }

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Functions and Arrays
lessons.html:
Lesson 3: Functions and Arrays

Functions in PHP are blocks of code that can be called multiple times with different arguments.

Defining a Function:

function greet($name) { return Hello,  . $name; }

Arrays:

Arrays allow you to store multiple values in a single variable.

$fruits = array(apple, banana, cherry);

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Creating REST API with PHP
lessons.html:
Lesson 5: Creating REST API

RESTful APIs allow different applications to communicate over HTTP.

HTTP Methods:

  • GET: Used to retrieve data.
  • POST: Used to create new data.

Example Code:

if ($_SERVER[REQUEST_METHOD] == GET) { /* handle GET requests */ }
